question: Which Mauryan Indian emperor is renowned for his edicts and pillars?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Ashoka**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Emperor Ashoka of the Mauryan Empire is renowned for his edicts and pillars:**
 
• Ashoka's edicts were inscriptions carved into stone pillars, boulders, and cave walls throughout India.
 
• These edicts provided insights into ancient India's history, culture, and governance.
 
• They included:
 
 
• Prohibition of animal sacrifice, especially during festive seasons
 
• Medical treatment of humans and animals
 
• Planting of fruits, medicinal herbs, and the digging of wells
 
 
 
• Ashoka's **edicts were made on the Pillars of Ashoka**.
 
• Ashoka ruled most of the Indian subcontinent from 268 BCE to 232 BCE.
 
• He was a highly influential promulgator of Indian Buddhism.
 
• His dhamma emphasized non-violence, mutual respect, and understanding between people of different sects and beliefs. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Harsha:
 
 
• Harsha, the ruler of the Vardhana dynasty (7th century CE), did issue coins, but they were primarily gold coins with his portrait, and he is famous for his patronage of Buddhism.
 
• His coins were more symbolic of his royal authority and religious support.
 
 
 
• Kanishka:
 
 
• Kanishka was a king of the Kushana dynasty (1st-2nd century CE), and he is one of the most prominent rulers known for issuing gold dinars.
 
• Kanishka’s gold coins were highly valued and important for the Kushana Empire's economy. T
 
• he coins featured various gods and symbols, and Kanishka was one of the key promoters of Buddhism.
 
 
 
• Samudragupta:
 
 
• Samudragupta, a ruler of the Gupta dynasty (4th-5th century CE), is famous for his gold coins.
 
• He is also known as a patron of the arts and for his military prowess.
 
• However, his coins were somewhat different in design, often depicting him as a warrior or seated in various poses of victory.
